battle.name: 法蒂瑪入侵埃及
battle.theater: 埃及北部（富斯塔特至亞歷山大）
battle.brief: 914年，法蒂瑪王朝哈里發曼蘇爾命將軍穆罕默德·本·伊薩率軍渡紅海入侵埃及，翌年奪取富斯塔特與尼羅河三角洲，隨後圍困亞歷山大至916年前後陷落，埃及自阿拔斯王朝易主。卡面投石機未隨軍而至，然此役所用拋射機正承羅馬扭力投石機的攻城邏輯，亞歷山大的城牆便在這條路線上被反覆試煉。

kit.name: 投石機
kit.history: 把絞盤的勢能換成一塊石頭。攻城從此有了可以計算的破壞力。

countries: 914年法蒂瑪入侵埃及，是伊斯馬歐里什亞派法蒂瑪政權第一次大規模出兵北非以外，目標是阿拔斯王朝最富庶的行省。交戰一方是法蒂瑪王朝：自909年阿爾·馬赫迪（Al-Mahdi）以喀什圖瑪柏柏爾人為主力攻下馬赫迪亞、另立政權以來，其政權以突尼斯為根據地，軍隊骨幹是從柏柏爾山區與南突尼斯招募的喀什圖瑪部族兵，輔以馬格里布自願歸附者、雇傭的突尼斯與地中海水手，以及部分從伊拉克起義的什葉派舊部。此次出征由第二任哈里發阿布·阿里·曼蘇爾（Al-Mansur）下令，由將軍穆罕默德·本·伊薩率領，指揮權集中於主將一身，後方由哈里發本人在馬赫迪亞與凱魯萬坐鎮，維持後勤與海上運輸。另一方是巴格達的阿拔斯王朝。當時的哈里發是穆克塔菲（al-Muktafi），帝國晚期對埃及維持直轄：埃及自八世紀以來一直是阿拔斯最重要的農業與稅收來源，穀物與稅金年年經海路運往哈里發都與兩座聖城。駐埃及總督艾哈邁德·本·穆達比爾（Ibn al-Mudabbir）以嚴酷理財著稱，卻缺乏能與法蒂瑪正面抗衡的兵威。命令體系上，阿拔斯方面的指揮鏈是巴格達哈里發—埃及總督—省級軍團；法蒂瑪方面的指揮鏈是哈里發—主將—各部族首領。兩條鏈的差別在於距離：阿拔斯的援軍要穿越敘利亞再沿地中海陸路南下，法蒂瑪的援軍則靠海船由馬格里布直航紅海，航程短得多。
countriesEn: The Fatimid invasion of Egypt of 914 was the first large-scale campaign the Isma'ili Fatimid state mounted outside North Africa, and its target was the richest province of the Abbasid caliphate. One side was the Fatimid dynasty: since 909, when al-Mahdi had taken Mahdia with the Kutama Berbers as his main strength and founded a state of his own, the regime had been based in Ifriqiya, and the backbone of its army was drawn from the Kutama clans of the Berber mountains and southern Tunisia, supported by volunteers from the Maghreb, hired Tunisian and Mediterranean sailors, and part of the Shi'i recruits who had risen in Iraq. The expedition was ordered by the second caliph, Abu Ali al-Mansur, and led by the general Muhammad ibn Isa; command authority was concentrated in the field commander, while the caliph himself remained in Mahdia and in Kairouan to sustain the supply lines and the sea transport. The other side was the Abbasid caliphate ruled from Baghdad, whose caliph in 914 was al-Muktafi. Egypt had been under direct Abbasid rule since the eighth century and remained the empire's most important source of agriculture and taxation, its grain and its revenue shipping every year to the caliph's capital and to the two holy cities. The governor of Egypt, Ahmad ibn al-Mudabbir, was celebrated for his harsh financial administration but possessed little military weight to face the Fatimids. On the Abbasid side the chain of command ran from the caliph in Baghdad through the governor in Egypt down to the provincial garrisons; on the Fatimid side it ran from the caliph through the field commander to the tribal leaders. The difference lay in distance: an Abbasid reinforcement had to march down through Syria and then along the Mediterranean coast, whereas the Fatimids' replacements came by sea straight from the Maghreb to the Red Sea, a far shorter passage.
people: 這場戰爭的關鍵人物集中在三處。哈里發阿布·阿里·曼蘇爾是阿爾·馬赫迪的弟弟，在其兄於910年去世後接掌法蒂瑪政權；正是他在911至915年間連續平定內部由阿拔斯暗中支持的柏柏爾系與阿拉伯系軍人叛亂，把北非的兵權重新收攏到哈里發手中，也才騰出力量東進埃及。他下達的出兵令帶有清楚的目的：拿下埃及即可切斷阿拔斯從埃及抽取的稅源與糧道，同時取得向東渡海、威脅麥加與麥地那的基地。將軍穆罕默德·本·伊薩是此役的統帥，此人原為宮廷太監出身，因在政變與平叛中屍建功業而升為法蒂瑪最可倚重的大將；他指揮大軍渡紅海、攻入埃及、圍困亞歷山大，是全役軍事層面的第一人物。傳記材料多稱其後由其子接任埃及總督之職，父子相繼，使法蒂瑪在埃及的統治未因主將更替而中斷。阿拔斯方面，總督艾哈邁德·本·穆達比爾是關鍵人物。他的財政手腕在巴格達被視為斂財之能臣，卻在戰局上被批評為缺乏軍略；法蒂瑪軍進入三角洲之後，他放棄富斯塔特，退往巴格達求援，把埃及的行政中樞拱手讓出。而在亞歷山大，真正決定城牆能否被突破的，是攻城一方的工程技師、操縱投射機的器械組與被徵調來修築壕溝、壅土與射擊陣地的勞役隊伍；拜占庭方面的觀察者則在編年中把這場戰爭的成敗記在法蒂瑪是否真正掌握亞歷山大這一條上。整體而言，此役是一場哈里發親自授權、將軍親自執行、對手指揮層在關鍵時刻失靈的典型遠征。
peopleEn: The decisive figures of this war fall into three groups. The caliph Abu Ali al-Mansur was the brother of al-Mahdi and took over the Fatimid state when his brother died in 910; it was he who put down, between 911 and 915, the Berber and Arab officer revolts in the interior that the Abbasids had been quietly encouraging, gathering the military authority of North Africa once more into the caliph's hands and only then finding the strength to march east into Egypt. The order he issued carried a plain purpose: to seize Egypt was to cut off the Abbasid revenue and grain that flowed from that province, and at the same time to gain a base from which to threaten Mecca and Medina across the Red Sea. The general Muhammad ibn Isa was the commander of the campaign. A palace eunuch by origin, he had risen through coups and suppressions of revolt into one of the Fatimids' most trusted captains, and he led the army across the Red Sea, into Egypt and up to the walls of Alexandria; he is the first military figure of the whole war. The narrative materials usually state that his son succeeded him as governor of Egypt, so that the Fatimid hold on Egypt was not interrupted by a change of commander. On the Abbasid side the key figure was the governor Ahmad ibn al-Mudabbir. His financial dexterity was treated in Baghdad as that of a master collector, but his generalship was criticised; once the Fatimid army entered the Delta he abandoned Fustat and fell back on Baghdad for help, handing over the administrative centre of the province. At Alexandria, what actually decided whether the walls would break was the engineering crews of the besiegers, the crews who manned the throwing engines, and the labour gangs conscripted to build trench, rampart and firing positions; the Byzantine observers, for their part, recorded in their chronicles that the whole issue turned on whether the Fatimids could actually hold Alexandria. In sum this was a textbook distant campaign: authorised by the caliph, executed by the general, and lost by the other side's command structure at the critical moment.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是投石機（Onager），羅馬人用扭力束蓄力的單臂拋石機，其公認形制在公元前二世紀已經成熟，並在羅馬－拜占庭世界沿用數百年。圍攻亞歷山大時真正在城牆外作戰的並非這種早期機型：法蒂瑪軍中使用的是從拜占庭與伊斯蘭技術譜系繼承的曳引式拋射機（阿拉伯史料常稱的吉拉丁一類機械），加上雲梯、撞槌、壕溝、壅土、柴垛與盾牆。但投石機在這條技術譜系上的位置不可取代：它確立了「把蓄勢的機械能換成一塊石頭、讓石頭以計算過的角度飛越城頭」的攻城邏輯，其後所有拋射機的設計——包括改用墜重代替扭力的版本——都只是在同一條路線上更換動力來源。羅馬人還留下一套可操作的工地制度：先量基腳，再夯實，然後立柱、上絞盤、裝臂、扣索、分段試射，這套程序在拜占庭與阿拉伯工兵手裡改頭換面地延續了幾百年。除攻城器械外，埃及與法蒂瑪雙方的野戰裝備也值得一提。埃及的守軍與法蒂瑪的柏柏爾步兵使用弓、矛、短劍與標槍，重裝與輕裝之間沒有絕對分界；柏柏爾騎兵善用高速衝鋒與投射武器，長矛騎兵則是法蒂瑪隊伍的骨幹。攻城一方還需要大量工程輔助器材：填壕用的柴捆與沙袋、防止守軍掘地道的壕溝支撐與濕土填塞、遮蔽弓箭手的攻城塔，以及把攻城機械從營地搬到城下的滾木與滑軌。海上運輸同樣關鍵：馬格里布與紅海之間的海路、尼羅河三角洲的內河船隊、連接法尤姆運河與沿河口岸的貨船，構成這次遠征真正的後勤骨架；武器、糧食與工匠，全部靠這條線送進來。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the onager, the single-armed stone-thrower in which the Roman engineers stored energy in twisted skeins of sinew; its recognised form was already mature in the second century BC and it stayed in Roman and Byzantine service for centuries. What actually worked against the walls of Alexandria in 914 was not that early type: the Fatimid besiegers used throwing engines inherited from the Byzantine and Islamic technical repertoire — the machines the Arabic sources call by the mangonel name — together with ladders, rams, ditches, earthen ramparts, fagots and mantlets. But the onager's place in that lineage cannot be replaced: it established the siege logic of turning stored mechanical energy into a single stone and sending that stone over the wallhead at a calculated angle, and every throwing engine designed afterwards — including the later types that substitute a dropping weight for torsion — merely changes the power source along the same line. The Romans also left behind a workable site discipline: survey the footing first, ram it hard, then raise the frame, mount the winches, fit the arm, strain the ropes and fire in tested stages, a procedure that passed through Byzantine and Arab engineers' hands for centuries with its form repeatedly changed. Besides the siege engines, the field equipment of both sides deserves notice. Egyptian garrisons and Fatimid Berber infantry used bows, spears, short swords and javelins, and there was no absolute dividing line between heavy and light; the Berber cavalry were skilled in the fast charge and in missile work, while the lance cavalry formed the backbone of the Fatimid order. The besiegers also needed a great deal of ancillary engineering material: brushwood bundles and sandbags for filling ditches, revetments and rammed earth to stop the garrison tunnelling, siege towers to shield the archers, and rollers and slides for hauling the engines forward from the camp to the walls. Sea transport mattered just as much: the sea lane between the Maghreb and the Red Sea, the river flotilla of the Nile Delta, and the cargo boats that fed the Fayyum canal and the riverside ports together formed the real logistical skeleton of this expedition. Weapons, grain and craftsmen all came in along that line.
tactics: 法蒂瑪軍的這次遠征是一場典型的兩段式攻勢：先取尼羅河三角洲與行政樞紐，再轉而對付真正難啃的亞歷山大城。渡海與入埃及一段刻意避開阿拔斯控制下的西奈陸路，主力自馬格里布出發後由海路抵達紅海沿岸港口，再循既有商道向西北進入尼羅河谷地；進入三角洲後，戰役節奏由一次成功的正面突破開啟——法蒂瑪騎兵與步兵在平坦的三角洲耕地上迅速壓倒對手，總督退往巴格達，富斯塔特易手，城中的星期五講道隨即改換內容。控制富斯塔特就等於握住尼羅河的糧食、磨坊與徵稅機關，遠征軍隊的給養問題至此解決，士氣亦隨之由「求取一城」轉為「攻城」。亞歷山大之圍則是另一種打法。守城方倚靠古羅馬時期留下的城牆體系與海港，而自七世紀阿拉伯人切斷通往法羅斯島的堤道之後，城的海上接近面長期受限，這正是法蒂瑪方敢分兵封鎖海面、以陸地圍城的前提。圍城工事包括：環城的壕溝、填土、柴垛與投石壘；沿牆展開的攻城塔與雲梯；以及把拋射機分批前推、交替掩體射擊的射擊陣地。攻城方同時處理三件難事：水源與糧草的持續供應、器械運轉所需的人力與絞盤的保養、以及防止守軍反擊破壞器械的盾牆與護壕。守軍則以反擊工程為主：修補缺口、拋擲燃燒物與投射物、夜間襲擊暴露在前的器械陣地，並盡量拖延到法蒂瑪遠征軍因糧秣與疲勞而自行鬆動。
tacticsEn: The Fatimid expedition of 914 followed a classic two-stage pattern: take the Nile Delta and its administrative hub first, then turn on the genuinely hard target, Alexandria. The movement by sea and the entry into Egypt deliberately avoided the overland route through Sinai held by the Abbasids; the main force set out from the Maghreb, reached the Red Sea ports by sea, and then followed the existing caravan tracks north-west into the Nile valley. Once in the Delta the tempo of the campaign was set by one successful breakthrough: Fatimid cavalry and infantry overran their opponents on the flat cultivated ground, the governor fell back on Baghdad, Fustat changed hands, and the Friday khutba in the mosque was reworded to name a different caliph. Holding Fustat meant holding the Nile's grain, its mills and its tax machinery, and the supply problem of the expeditionary army was thereby solved, while the mood of the troops shifted from the search for a prize to the business of a siege. The siege of Alexandria was a different kind of operation. The defenders relied on the wall circuit left behind by the Roman city and on the harbour, but since the Arabs cut the causeway to the island of Pharos in the seventh century the seaward approaches of the city had long been restricted, and that was precisely the premise on which the Fatimids dared to seal the sea with a detachment and to besiege the city by land. The siege works included a circumferential ditch, earthworks, fagots and a stone-throwing terrace; siege towers and ladders set along the walls; and firing positions from which the throwing engines were pushed forward in relays, firing in turn from covered positions. The besiegers had to manage three things at once: the continuous supply of water and food, the manpower needed to work the engines and the upkeep of the winches, and the mantlets and covered approaches that kept the garrison from breaking up the machines. The garrison, for its part, fought with the engineering of the counter-attack: mending the breaches, hurling incendiaries and missiles, striking at night at the engine positions left exposed in front of the wall, and holding out in the hope that the Fatimid army would loosen from want of food and from exhaustion.
data: 關於兵力，史料記載分歧很大，只能以範圍而非定數來看。法蒂瑪遠征軍的兵力，各家多記在兩萬上下，也有說法一萬餘乃至四萬；其中柏柏爾步兵為主體，騎兵與水手的比例各說不一。亞歷山大守軍的數目，史料留下的記載更少，通常只提到總督所部駐軍與雇傭守備，難以核實。時間跨度則相對清楚：遠征軍於914年出兵，915年控制富斯塔特與尼羅河三角洲，對亞歷山大的圍城自915年延續到916年，其後的接管與肅清又把戰役拖到918年，前後約四年。距離與地理是可以量化的：法尤姆到亞歷山大的陸路約二百公里，尼羅河三角洲的耕地在當時佔埃及可耕地的大部分，而亞歷山大城牆沿線的周長以公里計，古羅馬時期留下的城防環線遠長於任何一座中世紀歐洲城牆。攻城器械的運作亦有可推的量級：一具曳引式拋射機的拋程以數百公尺計，操作需要數十人同時拉索，兩具以上同時投射才可能在城頭形成壓制。另有兩組常被引用的數字：法蒂瑪在埃及的常駐軍，傳記多記為一萬上下；法蒂瑪自亞歷山大搬走的圖書，後來在突尼斯凱魯萬的曼蘇里亞宮形成以數十萬卷計的收藏，其中一份約百卷的書目流傳至今。年代框架也清楚：法蒂瑪建國於909年，佔領埃及始於914年，開羅建城要到969年，而阿拔斯王朝在巴格達的終局則是945年。
dataEn: On numbers the sources disagree badly, so they can only be given as ranges rather than as fixed figures. The strength of the Fatimid expedition is put by most writers at around twenty thousand, with estimates running from a little over ten thousand to forty thousand; Berber infantry formed the bulk of it, and the proportion of cavalry and of sailors varies from account to account. The number of the defenders of Alexandria is far less well recorded, the sources usually mentioning only the garrison of the governor and the hired defenders, and it cannot be checked. The time span is clearer: the expedition set out in 914, Fustat and the Delta were controlled in 915, the siege of Alexandria ran from 915 to 916, and the subsequent takeover and pacification dragged the campaign out to 918, four years in all. Distances and geography can be quantified: the road from the Fayyum to Alexandria is about two hundred kilometres, the cultivated land of the Nile Delta then made up the greater part of Egypt's arable area, and the perimeter of Alexandria's wall circuit is measured in kilometres, the Roman ring running far longer than the circuit of any medieval European city wall. The working of the siege engines can also be estimated in order of magnitude: a traction throwing engine had a range of several hundred metres, needed several dozen men pulling the ropes at once, and it took two or more engines firing together to place a real pressure on a wall head. Two further sets of figures are often quoted: the Fatimid garrison in Egypt is given in the narratives at about ten thousand men, and the books the Fatimids carried away from Alexandria later formed a collection counted in tens of thousands of volumes in the al-Mansuriyya palace at Kairouan in Tunisia, of which a catalogue of about a hundred volumes survives. The chronological frame is firm as well: the Fatimid state was founded in 909, the conquest of Egypt began in 914, Cairo was founded only in 969, and the Abbasid caliphate ended in Baghdad in 945.
cause: 法蒂瑪進攻埃及並非衝動之舉，而是建國之後被形勢逼出來的選擇。第一是財源：法蒂瑪是一個靠軍事征服迅速崛起的什葉派政權，卻坐擁北非最貧瘠的一片土地，銅料、稅收與兵源都遠不如阿拔斯；埃及卻是富庶的農業行省，穀物、稅金與織物年年經海路運往突尼斯。拿下埃及，等於為法蒂瑪裝上一個能自我供養的財政來源。第二是戰略：阿拔斯在敘利亞與伊拉克的邊境上長期壓制法蒂瑪，一旦法蒂瑪在東地中海取得埃及，就等於在阿拔斯的腹地插上一把刀，隨時可以沿地中海北上，也可以從紅海東進。第三是宗派與正統：曼蘇爾清楚地知道，奪取麥加與麥地那、接管兩座聖城的朝覲與什一稅，是打擊阿拔斯及其支持者最有效的宣教手段，而控制埃及是先決條件。第四是內部形勢：曼蘇爾上台時面對的是內亂，其軍隊的骨幹是柏柏爾部落的兵，這支兵一旦有了明確的敵人與奪取的目標，原先的叛亂傾向就會被收攏為進取的士氣，遠征本身即是安撫軍心之舉。第五是被佔領地的反動：阿拔斯在埃及的稅制與警察式治理素以嚴苛著稱，總督穆達比爾一系的攤派在地方上造成普遍不滿，這些不滿為法蒂瑪的策反與滲透提供了空間。綜合而言，914年的出兵是一場以軍力為後盾、以宗派為旗號、以財政與聖地為目標的攻勢。
causeEn: The Fatimid attack on Egypt was not an impulse but a choice forced on the new state by the shape of its position. First, revenue: the Fatimids were a Shi'i regime that had risen with startling speed on the strength of military conquest, yet they held some of the poorest land in North Africa, and in coin, taxes and man-power they were no match for the Abbasids; Egypt, by contrast, was a rich agricultural province whose grain, revenue and cloth moved by sea to Tunis every year. Taking Egypt meant fitting the Fatimids with a source of finance that could feed itself. Second, strategy: the Abbasids had long hemmed the Fatimids in along the Syrian and Iraqi frontier, and once the Fatimids held Egypt in the eastern Mediterranean they had a knife in the belly of the caliphate, able at any time to march north along the coast or east across the Red Sea. Third, sectarian legitimacy and orthodoxy: al-Mansur understood perfectly that seizing Mecca and Medina, and with them the pilgrimage and the alms owed to the two holy cities, was the most effective religious blow one could strike at the Abbasids and their partisans, and that control of Egypt was the precondition for it. Fourth, the internal situation: al-Mansur inherited a regime in turmoil, and the backbone of his army was Berber tribal fighting men, who, given a clear enemy and a prize worth taking, converted a predisposition to mutiny into offensive spirit — the expedition itself was a device for settling the troops. Fifth, the disaffection of the occupied land: Abbasid taxation and police government in Egypt were notorious for harshness, and the levies of the governor's family created widespread local resentment, which gave Fatimid agents room to work. Taken together, the dispatch of 914 was an offensive backed by military force, flying the banner of sect, and aimed at treasury and holy city alike.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果超出埃及一省。首先，阿拔斯王朝失去它在藩屬中最富庶的一個行省。埃及的稅收曾支撐著哈里發都的日常開支與對邊防的津貼，失去之後，阿拔斯的財政基礎出現長期裂縫，帝國權威在西部與南部加速鬆動；945年布依亞德家族攻入巴格達、廢黜阿拔斯哈里發，與這道裂縫直接相關。其次，法蒂瑪取得地中海東岸與紅海的交會點，把突尼斯的地中海基地與紅海航線連成一條完整通路；從此法蒂瑪的艦隊可以在西西里與義大利南部任意巡航，與同樣想控制地中海的拜占庭形成長期對峙，兩者之間最激烈的一役便是965年法蒂瑪艦隊進攻西西里。第三，埃及的轉手改變了北非的權力版圖，把法蒂瑪從一個北非王國推成地中海強權；969年賈希爾·西基利在法蒂瑪王室推動下於法尤姆另建新都，其後遷都開羅，埃及從此成為法蒂瑪的權力核心與薩法維王朝反攻的基地。第四，知識與技術層面的影響更為深遠：法蒂瑪自亞歷山大帶走大批古籍，運回凱魯萬的曼蘇里亞宮，構成伊斯蘭世界最早的大型宮廷藏書之一，與同時期巴格達智慧宮的命運形成對照——後者在十二世紀蒙古西征中散佚，前者則成為後來開羅知識傳統的源頭之一。第五，科普特教會在阿拔斯保護下形成的自治安排被法蒂瑪接管又改造，其處境在第十世紀持續變化，直至法蒂瑪王朝在十一世紀末的十字軍時期向基督教勢力求援。總之，914年之後，埃及不再屬於哈里發，而屬於一個以法蒂瑪為名的新秩序。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reached far beyond the single province. First, the Abbasid caliphate lost the richest of its provinces. Egyptian revenue had supported the daily expenses of the caliph's court and the pay of the frontier garrisons; once it was gone, a long fissure opened in the Abbasid financial base and the empire's authority loosened quickly in the west and the south. The Buyid family's entry into Baghdad in 945 and the deposition of the Abbasid caliph stand in direct connection with that fissure. Second, the Fatimids gained the meeting point of the eastern Mediterranean and the Red Sea, joining their Tunisian base to the Red Sea route into a single line; from then on the Fatimid fleets could cruise at will off Sicily and southern Italy, forming a long confrontation with Byzantium, which wanted the same sea, and the sharpest single episode of that rivalry was the Fatimid expedition against Sicily in 965. Third, the transfer of Egypt redrew the balance of power in North Africa and pushed the Fatimids from being a North African kingdom to being a Mediterranean power; in 969, at the Fatimid court's prompting, Jawhar al-Siqilli founded a new capital in the Fayyum, and after the move to Cairo, Egypt became the power centre of the Fatimids and the base from which the Safavids later struck back. Fourth, the effect on knowledge and technique went deeper still: the Fatimids carried great numbers of books away from Alexandria to the al-Mansuriyya palace at Kairouan, forming one of the earliest great palace libraries of the Islamic world, a striking contrast with the fate of the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, which was scattered by the Mongol incursions of the thirteenth century, while the Kairouan collection became one of the sources of Cairo's later scholarly tradition. Fifth, the autonomous arrangements that the Coptic Church had known under Abbasid protection were taken over and reshaped by the Fatimids, and its position kept changing through the tenth century until the Fatimid court, in the time of the Crusades at the end of the eleventh century, called on Christian powers for help. In sum, after 914 Egypt belonged no longer to the caliph but to a new order that bore the name of the Fatimids.
result: 到918年，法蒂瑪王朝完成了對埃及的接管：亞歷山大在圍攻之後陷落，富斯塔特成為法蒂瑪在埃及的行政治所，埃及的星期五講道改念法蒂瑪哈里發的名號，阿拔斯的官吏被逐一撤換，伊斯馬歐里什亞派在埃及建立了自己的稅制與軍制。這一結果對阿拔斯而言是一場戰略失敗的公開實錄：哈里發仍在巴格達的宮殿裡維持著虛名，而整個尼羅河流域已經易幟。法蒂瑪這一邊也不是沒有代價。長期的遠征與圍城消耗了從北非抽調出來的兵員，曼蘇爾本人在911年後的內鬥中已經精疲力竭，佔領埃及並未讓他再進一步攻取兩座聖城；其後十餘年阿拔斯曾企圖把埃及奪回，雙方在邊境與地中海反覆拉鋒，而埃及的佔領始終維持。法蒂瑪最終把首都留在北非，把埃及當作東翼的基地，這一取向直到969年之後才被放棄——開羅建成後，政權中心東移，埃及從戰利品變成根基。就兵器與戰術而言，此役留下的最大遺產是攻城技術的東移與轉化：羅馬人留下的投石機式樣，經拜占庭的改進後落入阿拉伯世界，隨後在十字軍時代被複製並放大成配重式巨弩。亞歷山大的城牆最終並非被某一具器械攻破——圍城的勝負最後是由糧秣、封鎖、人心與時間共同決定的，但攻城器械在其中的位置，已經從羅馬時代的「計算破壞力」走到了中世紀的「持續壓制」。
resultEn: By 918 the Fatimid dynasty had completed its takeover of Egypt: Alexandria had fallen after the siege, Fustat became the administrative seat of the Fatimids in Egypt, the Friday khutba in the mosques was changed to name the Fatimid caliph, the Abbasid officials were replaced one by one, and the Isma'ili sect established its own fiscal and military system in the province. For the Abbasids this was the public record of a strategic failure: the caliph still kept up the appearance of rule in the palaces of Baghdad while the whole Nile valley had changed hands. The Fatimids paid for it too. A long expedition and a long siege had drained the troops drawn out of North Africa, al-Mansur himself was exhausted by the internal struggles that had followed 911, and the occupation of Egypt did not bring him on to attack the two holy cities; for more than a decade afterwards the Abbasids tried to retake Egypt, the two sides pulling at each other along the frontier and across the sea, and the Fatimid possession was never seriously shaken. The Fatimids kept their capital in North Africa for the time being and treated Egypt as a base on their eastern wing; that arrangement was only abandoned after 969, when the founding of Cairo moved the centre of power eastward and Egypt changed from a prize into a foundation. As for arms and siegecraft, the great inheritance of this war is the eastward transmission and transformation of siege technology: the form the Romans gave the onager, improved by the Byzantines, passed into the Arab world and was then copied and enlarged in the Crusader age into the great counterweight trebuchet. The walls of Alexandria were in the end not broken by any single engine — the outcome of a siege is decided in the end by food, blockade, morale and time together — but the position of the siege engine within it had already moved from the Roman age of calculated destructive power to the medieval age of sustained pressure.
